subject: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal

Markus —

Quick summary: Acme Payments (Sarah/Greg on copy) have signaled they will execute an enterprise contract if we deliver two items before their legal/finance board signs next month: (1) a scheduled, signed billing export to their S3 with a per-invoice CSV that includes token-level metering, and (2) support for customer-managed KMS encryption for stored billing artifacts (CMK). These are hard asks from their CFO (they called it out explicitly).

Attached is the latest mutual action plan and a short SAML/export spec that outlines the required fields. The commercial team needs a firm commitment (ETA + high-level engineering approach) by end of week so procurement can align with DocuSign timelines.

Ask: can Product/Eng evaluate prioritizing a small scoped implementation that meets the CFO's requirements (export + CMK + simple verification handshake) as a Q3 sprint item or a short-lifecycle spike with a canary? We are prepared to accept a phased approach if you prefer: phase 1 = scheduled export + CSV schema, phase 2 = CMK + audit hooks.

If there's any immediate blocker (security, infra cost, cross-region replication), call it out and we can raise a change request with the customer to accept a short-term workaround (manual export) for a limited period.

Attachments: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.pdf (PDF), SAML_Billing_Export_Spec.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks — would appreciate a quick read and ETA.

—Karthik
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask and the docs. A few clarifying questions before I scope with the team:

1) Volume: what is the expected monthly invoice count and peak token volume per invoice? That affects export batching and S3 lifecycle costs.
2) CMK requirement: is the ask that each exported file be encrypted with a customer key (their KMS ARN) at rest, or is it acceptable for us to encrypt in-transit and store under our key while delivering an encrypted copy to the customer's S3?
3) SLA: when you say the CFO needs this for the signature, do they require a formal SLA addendum (latency/availability) or just a contractual clause that we will deliver the integration?

Possible short-term workaround: we can offer a managed nightly export (CSV) via a segregated pipeline and deliver to their S3 with server-side encryption using their bucket policy. That avoids touching CMK for phase 1 but would still meet finance needs.

I'll book a 30-minute sync with Platform and Security for Thursday to walk through feasibility. If the numbers are modest (sub-100k invoices/month), I think we can do a spike in a two-week cycle and propose a minimal-first-cut implementation. If it's north of that, we'll need to plan for batching and cost controls.

—Markus
VP, Product
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-pay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal

Looping to be blunt: Acme will sign by 7/30 if they have a written commitment with ETA. Procurement has a legal window that closes the last week of July. We can't stretch this beyond early August without losing momentum. Sales is offering a $1.2M ARR starting Q4, this is significant.

If Product can give a firm canary date (even an engineering spike/POC acceptance criteria) by Friday COB, we'll push to get the legal commitment to the board. If Product needs roadmap swaps, let's discuss what we can trade (e.g., we can delay a non-customer-facing internal telemetry cleanup item).

—Monica
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-pay.com>, Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@acme-pay.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal

Markus — answers inline and added a short note on usage: see quoted thread.

On 13 Jul 2026 Markus Klein wrote:
> 1) Volume: what is the expected monthly invoice count and peak token volume per invoice?

ACME estimate: ~45k invoices/month initially, expect up to 120k within 12 months. Avg tokenized usage per invoice export ~8k tokens (after compression), peak up to 50k for larger enterprise invoices.

> 2) CMK requirement: is the ask that each exported file be encrypted with a customer key (their KMS ARN) at rest, or is it acceptable for us to encrypt in-transit and store under our key while delivering an encrypted copy to the customer's S3?

Customer preference is CMK at rest on their S3 bucket. They indicated compliance requires ownership of key lifecycle. They are open to a hybrid approach if we can demonstrate the exported files are encrypted with their key on the destination side and we provide audit logs proving delivery.

> 3) SLA: when you say the CFO needs this for the signature, do they require a formal SLA addendum (latency/availability) or just a contractual clause that we will deliver the integration?

They want a contractual commitment: an integration delivery ETA and a 99.9% delivery SLA for export jobs (monthly) with audit logs retained for 12 months. Legal is OK with a phased SLA (soft SLA for phase 1, formal SLA after phase 2).

I've attached a redline-ready contract excerpt the customer circulated (Contract_Redlines.docx).

If Platform/Security need more time, ask for what you need specifically — we can request a two-week POC window the customer will accept.

—Karthik
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.example.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.example.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@acme-pay.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CFO integration & billing export — prioritization ask for ACME deal

Thanks — good context. Next steps from Product/Platform side: 

- We'll run a 10-business-day spike starting 7/19 to validate: (a) scheduled export pipeline with the requested CSV schema, (b) S3 delivery with customer's KMS applied at the destination and end-to-end delivery verification. Spike deliverables = POC export job, security checklist, and an internal runbook.
- If the spike validates, we will plan a Q3 sprint to harden and deliver a phased rollout: phase 1 (export + verification) targeted for 8/20; phase 2 (full CMK lifecycle integration + audit log retention) targeted for 9/17.
- We will need a temporary resource allocation from Sales/CS to help with acceptance criteria and on-call validation during the POC week (Monica/Jordan to coordinate).
- Risk: if the monthly volume climbs >100k before phase 1 completes, we will need to add a small scaling budget. We'll surface that as an optional committed spend in the Spike report.

I'll capture this plan in a short PRD and share by Friday. Karthik/Monica — if you need a firmer ETA for the legal team, tell me what slack we have on the canary date; otherwise I will communicate the above timeline to Acme.

—Markus
VP, Product
